answer:
Here is what I found, most urgent first. Your most recent record is dated July 14, 2026, so anything after that is not in what I have.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide (a water pill). Kestrel Harbor Hospital stopped it on March 5, 2026. Your sodium had fallen to 123, and you were admitted with dizziness after a fall at home. The discharge instructions say to stop it. But the pharmacy refilled it on April 2, 2026 with two refills left, and it still shows as active. On May 14 you told the eye clinic you were taking it, and your sodium on June 15 was still a little low (134). Your clinic's June 15 note says to continue current medications. Please call Dr. Marsh and the pharmacy this week to confirm whether you should be taking it. If it is stopped, ask for the refills to be cancelled, and ask whether your blood pressure plan needs changing. Seek urgent care for confusion, severe headache, vomiting, or fainting.

2. Lung nodule. A CT on October 18, 2025 (done for the kidney stone) found an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the right lower lung. The radiologist recommended a non-contrast chest CT in 6 to 12 months. That window ended October 18, 2026, and your records contain no chest CT. Being a never-smoker lowers the risk, but the recommendation still needs to be scheduled or deliberately declined.

3. Kidney stone follow-up. A 4 mm stone sits at the right ureter junction, and the urine test showed large blood. The instructions said to see your primary doctor within a week, and to see urology if the stone had not passed in two weeks. Your records show no urology visit, no repeat urine test, and no note confirming the stone passed.

4. Thyroid recheck. TSH was 7.9 (high) on March 3, 2026, with a normal free T4 (1.0). The hospital asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated 6 to 8 weeks after discharge, which is about late April. No repeat is recorded.

5. Cholesterol and a statin. On September 22, 2025 your LDL was 142 (high), HDL 48 (low), and triglycerides 155 (high). You have had type 2 diabetes since September 2025. No statin appears on any medication list, and there is no cholesterol test after September 2025. Guidelines usually recommend a statin for adults with diabetes in your age range, so ask whether one was discussed.

6. Vaccines. The pharmacy gave you a flu shot, the first Shingrix (shingles) dose, and Prevnar 20 on November 8, 2025. The second Shingrix dose was due 2 to 6 months later and is not recorded. Your clinic's copy lists only the October 2024 flu shot, so it may not have the November vaccines. There is no 2026-27 flu shot and no COVID-19 vaccine in any record.

7. Lists that do not match. Lisinopril was stopped in September 2025 for a dry cough. Only your clinic's copy records it as an intolerance. The hospital, eye clinic and pharmacy allergy lists show only aspirin. The aspirin reaction (hives) was recorded as mild in April 2025 and as moderate from May 2025 on. Ask them to correct both.

8. Refills. Losartan, metformin and amlodipine were last filled June 28, 2026 for 90 days, so the supply runs out around late September. I cannot see anything after July 14, so check that you have refills.

9. Diabetes. Your A1c has come down from 6.9% to 6.7% to 6.6% (June 15, 2026). Your eye exam on May 14, 2026 showed no diabetic retinopathy. Two gaps: no urine albumin test is recorded since diagnosis, and the yearly kidney urine check is missing. Your kidney function (eGFR 71) is normal. The next A1c is due around December 2026.

10. Screenings not in these records. No mammogram or cervical screening appears. Your colonoscopy in April 2019 was normal, so the next one is due around 2029.

What looks fine: your potassium has been normal throughout, and your June 2026 blood pressure of 128/80 was at goal. This is a summary of your records and general guidelines, not a diagnosis. Your doctors can confirm each item.
short: Ask about the water pill hydrochlorothiazide: the hospital stopped it in March 2026 for low sodium, but it still shows as active at your pharmacy and clinic, and your sodium was still low in June. Also ask about the 7 mm lung nodule CT (recommended by October 18, 2026, and not in your records), the thyroid recheck, and a statin.
